title: First-principles investigation of Na2TlSbY6 (Y=Cl, Br) compounds for high-performance photovoltaic applications

segments.text: The double perovskite halides Na2TlSbY6 (Y=Cl, Br) have emerged as promising materials for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications owing to their high structural symmetry, thermodynamic stability and environmentally benign elemental composition.

These compounds crystallize in a face-centered cubic (FCC) structure with the space group Fm-3m, where Tl and Sb cations are ordered in a rock-salt-type arrangement within a BX6 octahedral framework, forming a three-dimensional network of corner-sharing TlY6 and SbY6 octahedral stabilized by Na+ interstitials.

Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the optimized lattice constants for Na2TlSbCl6 and Na2TlSbBr6 are 10.628 & Aring; and 11.012 & Aring;, respectively, with the larger lattice constant for the bromide variant attributed to the larger ionic radius of Br-.
The compounds exhibit negative formation energies (-3.54 eV for Na2TlSbCl6 and -3.21 eV for Na2TlSbBr6), confirming their thermodynamic stability.
Mechanical properties indicate that Na2TlSbBr6 is slightly stiffer, with higher bulk and shear moduli compared to Na2TlSbCl6.

The calculated band gaps of 2.71eV for Na2TlSbCl6 and 2.43eV for Na2TlSbBr6 suggest that the bromide compound has extended absorption into the visible range, making it more suitable for solar energy applications.
The compounds exhibit indirect band gaps, with a favorable electronic structure that suggests high carrier mobility, supported by low effective masses of electrons and holes.
Optical properties reveal strong dielectric response and refractive index behavior, with both materials showing potential for applications in photodetectors, light-emitting diodes and solar cells.
These findings highlight the potential of Na2TlSbY6 halide perovskites as environmentally friendly and efficient materials for next-generation optoelectronic and photovoltaic technologies.

title: Influence of six different RE3+ ions as modifier agents on the photoluminescent, electrical, magnetic and thermal properties of B-Na glass

segments.text: This study deals with investigation of the influence of rare-earth (RE3+) ions La3+, Nd3+, Gd3+, Ho3+, Er3+, and Yb3+ on the structural, photoluminescent, electrical, and thermal properties of a simple 50%B2O3 - 50%Na2O glass system.
The incorporation of 1 mol% RE2O3 systematically enhanced optical polarizability, as indicated by the increase in molar refraction (R-m) and nonlinear susceptibility (chi((3))).
The Er3+ doped glass is exhibiting the highest value of chi((3)) approximate to 1.76 x 10(-12) esu.
The calculated optical basicity, oxide ion polarizability, and metallization criteria confirmed the nonmetallic nature of all compositions.

RE addition markedly intensified the photoluminescence emission, particularly for Gd3+ (> 2000 a.u.) and Er3+ (similar to 700 a.u.), accompanied by high correlated color temperature values (CCT > 7600 K).

Thermal analyses (TGA/DSC) revealed excellent stability up to 800 degrees C, with T-g values increasing from 422 degrees C (base glass) to 450 degrees C depending on RE type; the Nd3+-doped glass showed the highest thermal stability (Delta T approximate to 120 degrees C), implying superior glass-forming ability.
All RE-doped samples displayed paramagnetic behavior, except La3+-doped, which remained diamagnetic.

The dc conductivity decreased with decreasing ionic radius, consistent with the correlated barrier hopping (CBH) mechanism, while thermal conductivity (0.49-1.78 W m(-1) K-1) confirmed their insulating and thermoelectric potential.

Overall, the results demonstrate that RE3+ ions effectively tailor multifunctional characteristics of sodium borate glasses, highlighting their promise for advanced photonic and energy-related applications.

title: First-principles calculations to investigate structural, elastic and electronic properties of chloro-perovskite NaMgCl3

segments.text: In this work, we have investigated the structural, electronic, and optical properties of the halideperovskite NaMgCl3 by performing first-principles calculations using a mixed basis of the fullpotential linearized augmented plane wave (FP-LAPW) approach under the generalized gradient approximation (GGA-PBEsol), a revised Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof, and the modified Becke-Johnson (TB-mBJ) implemented on the Wien2k package.
The obtained results show that NaMgCl3 is more stable in the nonmagnetic phase.
The compound is found to be thermodynamically and elastically stable.
It is found that there is a good agreement between the calculated lattice constants and the values published in previous studies.
The complete set of first-order elastic constants tensor has been calculated, implying mechanical stability.
The Young's modulus, shear modulus, Poisson's ratio,Pugh's ratio, and universal anisotropy index have been additionally calculated.
The atomic bonds along both x and y axis are stronger than those along the z-axis.
The Debye temperature is calculated using the average sound velocity.
From electronic band structures, we have found that NaMgCl3 is an insulator with a direct wide band gap Gamma(V)->Gamma(C).
The electronic charge densities were plotted.
Analysis of the charge density distribution map reveals that the bondings in NaMgCl3 are ionic.

The calculated density of states (DOS) indicates that the valence band is mainly dominated by Cl- anions, the conduction band is mainly dominated by Mg2+ cations, whereas Na+ has a negligible contribution.
The optical characteristics, notably the dielectric function tensor, refractive function, reflectivity, absorption coefficient, photo-conductivity and transmittance were plotted and discussed.
The optical properties confirm that NaMgCl3 is optically anisotropic in 10-24 eV range .

The low transmittance and high absorption coefficient in the far ultra-violet region, between 90 and 250 nm, make this compound a good candidate for use as an ultraviolet shield, in vacuum ultraviolet lenses and in thermoelectric promising features due to his direct wide band gap.
Experimental and theoretical data are scarce for this compound in an ilmenite-type structure.

context_quotes: The low transmittance and high absorption coefficient in the far ultra-violet region, between 90 and 250 nm, make this compound a good candidate for use as an ultraviolet shield, in vacuum ultraviolet lenses and in thermoelectric promising features due to his direct wide band gap.
